alex-cust: Hey team — around 2026-02-10T18:05Z our dedicated pool (tn-123) started returning 429s and increased latency for long-context generation. Started right after a heavy batch of doc ingestion. Seeing lots of KV_EVICT and KV_ALLOC_FAIL in logs. Can you help?
jen-support: Sorry about the hit — escalating. Can you paste tenant id, a couple of example request IDs, and typical context size? Any recent config changes? :thinking:
alex-cust: tenant=tn-123, sample reqs: req_01F7a2, req_01F7a3. Typical inputs are ~35-45k tokens (doc + history). No config changes on our side, we ramped traffic 3x for a new experiment. Attaching a short log excerpt: 
```
2026-02-10T18:05:12.123Z WARN  runtime kvcache.go:412 KV_EVICT tenant=tn-123 slab=3 freed=184320 keys=12 prefix=doc:chunk:xyz
2026-02-10T18:05:12.124Z INFO  runtime alloc.go:88 KV_ALLOC_FAIL tenant=tn-123 req=req_01F7a2 need=220k avail=128k
2026-02-10T18:05:12.125Z INFO  runtime request.go:210 429 tenant=tn-123 req=req_01F7a2 route=dedicated-12 reason=kvcache-alloc-failure
```
ops-bot: alert: [KV_CACHE_PRESSURE] tn-123 high pressure (evict-rate=420/s, fragmentation=71%) at 2026-02-10T18:05:13Z
maya-sre: Hmm — logs + high frag number smell like aggressive eviction due to prefix skew / "ghost prefixes". If many slightly-different prefixes are created by chunking docs, slabs fragment and small free slots can't satisfy large KV allocations. Can you run kvcache stats and slab view? Try: 
```
redwoodctl kvcache stats --tenant tn-123 --window 15m
# or to capture slabs
redwoodctl kvcache slabs --tenant tn-123 --output table
```
alex-cust: ran the first one, pasted output below: 
```
tenant: tn-123
window: 15m
slabs_total: 8
slabs_in_use: 6
slab_bytes_total: 512MB
slab_bytes_free: 146MB
fragmentation_pct: 71.8
hot_key_count: 1341
prefix_skew: 0.82
evict_rate_per_s: 412
avg_kv_item_size: 18KB
```
maya-sre: OK that matches. High fragmentation + high avg item size. Two immediate mitigations to try: 1) Reduce per-request max_context (or use chunking server-side) so we store fewer huge entries; 2) Temporarily enable kvcache-compact job for this tenant and/or bump their kvcache_quota while we debug. Also collect a pprof from the runtime that serves tn-123 around the spike.
sam-runtime: Agreed. Also this looks like ghost-prefix churn — many keys with similar prefixes but unique suffixes prevent coalescing. Quick steps I recommend: 
- Run `redwoodctl kvcache compact --tenant tn-123` (non-disruptive but CPU-heavy)
- If pressure persists, set tenant eviction_policy=aggressive-compact or temporarily route tenant to a pool with larger slab allocation
- Add short-term routing rule to route long-context requests for tn-123 to fallback model `redwood-32k-lite` (smaller per-item KV footprint)
Example compact command & status check: 
```
redwoodctl kvcache compact --tenant tn-123 --concurrency 4
redwoodctl kvcache status --tenant tn-123
# watch logs: runtime kvcache: compact started slab=3
```
sam-runtime: For repro (eng-runtime): run synthetic load that mimics customer chunking pattern — many large items with near-identical prefixes: 
```
# pseudo repro
for i in 1..500 {
  POST /v1/generate
  body: { model: "redwood-long-32k", input: "<doc_chunk_prefix:X>" + random_suffix(8k) }
}
# parallel 200 connections for 2-3m
# capture evict_rate, fragmentation, slab usage during run
```
jen-support: I'm coordinating with billing/entitlements to temporarily increase the tenant kvcache_quota and with infra to prioritize the compact job. Also creating ticket INC-2026-834 to track. Will post updates. :thumbsup:
alex-cust: We applied a temporary change to reduce max_context to 20k on our side and traffic normalized after ~8 minutes. Evict rate dropped to ~30/s and errors stopped. Thank you everyone.
maya-sre: Glad that helped. We'll follow up with a root-cause action: (1) analyze prefix/key shape and consider server-side normalization for chunk keys, (2) default heuristics for compaction when fragmentation > 60% + evict_rate > 200/s, (3) docs for tenants on chunking best practices. Assigning follow-up to eng-runtime (sam-runtime).
sam-runtime: I'll take it. I'll run repro in staging, gather pprofs and a compaction perf run, and propose a runtime change to detect ghost prefixes and trigger targeted compaction.
jen-support: Closing escalation for now but keeping INC-2026-834 open for follow-up tasks. alex-cust: please reopen if you see any regression.
alex-cust: Will do — thanks again!
